pros: Logarithmic time for both range queries and point/range updates O(log n)
Versatile: supports any associative operation (sum, min, max, gcd, xor, etc.)
Lazy propagation enables efficient range updates (add, set, multiply)
Deterministic: height is always ⌈log₂ n⌉ regardless of input
Can be built in O(n) time (bottom-up construction)
Supports coordinate compression for sparse data
Foundation for advanced variants (persistent, 2D, segment tree beats)
Predictable memory usage: at most 4n nodes
Excellent for static data with frequent queries (RMQ, RSQ)
Can be augmented with additional information per node
cons: Requires O(n) space — 4× the input array size
More complex to implement than Fenwick tree for prefix queries
Range updates require lazy propagation (additional complexity)
Recursive implementation can cause stack overflow for large n
Not suitable for dynamic arrays (insertion/deletion in middle)
Constant factor 4× memory overhead even for small arrays
Building tree takes O(n) time (unacceptable for rarely-queried data)
Coordinate compression needed for large value ranges
Lazy propagation code is error-prone (multiple lazy types)
Tree structure depends on fixed n (hard to resize)
Not cache-optimal for very large trees (height > cache depth)
